name: International Pinot Noir Celebration
summary: Annual gathering of Pinot noir producers from around the world, held on the Linfield campus in McMinnville. It was envisioned in 1985 by Oregon winemakers, restaurateurs and retailers, and the first event took place in 1987.

sources.title: Celebrating 25 years of the IPNC (Tim Atkin)

name: Steamboat Pinot Noir Conference
summary: Annual technical gathering of Pinot noir winemakers from Oregon and California, conceived in 1979 and first held at the Steamboat Inn in 1980. After four years of planned rotation it settled permanently at the Steamboat Inn in the Umpqua Valley.

sources.title: The Legacy of Steamboat (Prince of Pinot)
Steamboat Conference History, by Stephen J. Cary (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Oregon Pinot Camp
summary: Invitation-only educational program, founded in 2000, that brings restaurant and retail wine buyers to Oregon for workshops hosted by Willamette Valley wineries.

sources.title: Q and A: David Adelsheim (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Gault-Millau Wine Olympics (1979)
summary: Tasting organized by the French magazine Gault-Millau in Paris in 1979. The 1975 Eyrie Vineyards Reserve Pinot noir from Oregon placed in the top ten in the Pinot noir competition.

name: Drouhin rematch tasting (1980)
summary: Follow-up blind tasting organized by Robert Drouhin at Maison Joseph Drouhin the year after the Wine Olympics. Drouhin's 1959 Chambolle-Musigny came first and the 1975 Eyrie Reserve Pinot noir second, two-tenths of a point behind.

name: International Cool Climate Symposium for Viticulture and Enology
summary: International research symposium series on cool-climate grape growing and winemaking, first created in 1984 by Oregon State University's Agricultural Experiment Station scientists and since held in cool-climate regions around the world.

sources.title: OSU scientists help Oregon's vineyards and wineries stay competitive (Oregon's Agricultural Progress, OSU)
Legacy remembered: Dr David Heatherbell (Rural News Group, New Zealand Winegrower)

name: Oregon Senate Bill 100 (1973)
aka: Oregon Land Conservation and Development Act of 1973
summary: The 1973 Oregon Land Conservation and Development Act, signed by Governor Tom McCall on 29 May 1973, which required county growth-management plans and the protection of farmland. Winegrowers led by David Adelsheim and David Lett mapped prime hillside vineyard land in the northern Willamette Valley and lobbied county planners to keep it from residential development.

sources.title: Oregon Land Conservation and Development Act of 1973 (Wikipedia)
Yamhill Area Land Use Map (Oregon History Project, Oregon Historical Society)
Land Use Planning Maps: David Adelsheim Collection (Linfield University)

name: Oregon wine labeling regulations (1977)
summary: Strict wine labeling rules adopted by the Oregon Liquor Control Commission in 1977, written and promoted by David Adelsheim over the preceding five years. They set a higher varietal minimum than federal law and barred borrowed place names.

sources.title: Knudsen Erath Brochure (Oregon History Project, Oregon Historical Society)

name: Carbon Neutral Challenge
summary: Carbon-reduction program for Oregon wineries run jointly by the Oregon Environmental Council and the Oregon Wine Board from 2007 to 2009; fourteen wineries completed it.

sources.title: 2007-2009: 20% of Oregon's wineries reduced their carbon footprint through our Carbon Neutral Challenge (Oregon Environmental Council)
Oregon eco-winery goes beyond LEED (National Geographic)

name: Oregon Wine Symposium
summary: Annual two-day educational conference and trade show for the Oregon wine industry, held each February in Portland and produced by the Oregon Wine Board and the Oregon Winegrowers Association.

name: One Barrel Challenge
summary: Charity release for Oregon Wine Month in May 2021 in which seven Oregon wineries each bottled a wine under a shared label, with all proceeds going to the Maurice Lucas Foundation.
